rules.title: Security deposit capped at first month's rent
rules.requirement: Your landlord cannot charge a security deposit larger than one month's rent, must put it in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, and must give you a signed statement of the apartment's condition. If the state housing office issues regulations, a landlord may offer an optional fee in lieu of a deposit, and deposit plus fees can never exceed one month's rent in total.

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days; interest; treble damages
rules.requirement: Your landlord must return your security deposit, minus only unpaid rent/water charges, allowed tax escalation, or documented damage beyond normal wear and tear, within 30 days after you move out, and must pay you yearly interest on it. If the landlord fails to return it on time, you can sue for three times the amount owed plus court costs and attorney's fees.

rules.title: Limit on upfront charges, including payments to landlord's agent (broker fees)
rules.requirement: At or before move-in, a landlord or the landlord's agent can only require you to pay first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of up to one month's rent, and the cost of a new lock and key. Since August 1, 2025, this also bars requiring you to pay the landlord's agent (such as the landlord's broker) anything beyond those items.
